proposal.for: the primary/supervisor - needs arrival-list admission before any lane or worker may land it
proposal.file: src/repository_presenter/components/readme/composition/planning.py::plan_checks (the per-capability title-vs-citation loop, ~lines 655-679) and, for consistency, authoring.py::unit_checks (~lines 1099-1118), which shares the identical standard by item 82's own design
proposal.root_cause: The rejection message plan_checks emits ('cite the facts that support this title, or title the capability by what it cites') states the RULE but names no candidate fact the model could actually cite - unlike, say, a fact-ID enum that constrains what a decoder may emit at all. With only one re-ask budgeted per job (core/llm/jobs.py, universal, not proposed for change here), a model correcting two simultaneous violations has to independently rediscover which of potentially hundreds of facts would satisfy each one, in one shot, with no gradient beyond the abstract instruction - as measured, it can manage a title-only fix (dropping the unsupported term) more reliably than a citation-add fix (finding the one supporting fact among 735) within that single try.
proposal.proposed_shape: When plan_checks (and unit_checks) finds a title term unsupported by the capability's own citations, look up which SUPPORTED facts elsewhere in the document DO carry that exact term (the same `facts.by_kind`-style scan plan_checks already had before item 82, now repurposed only for the error MESSAGE, never for the pass/fail verdict) and name up to a few of their fact IDs in the rejection string, e.g. '...which the facts it cites do not carry; cite one of format:input.eps, example:004 (which do), or title the capability by what it cites'. This changes no pass/fail boundary and weakens nothing - the verdict logic (item 82's fix) is untouched; only the re-ask's actionability improves, the same shape as the packet-enum fixes (items 40/55/59) that let a model cite instead of invent, applied to an error message instead of a schema.
proposal.explicitly_not_proposed: NO increase to the one-re-ask budget in core/llm/jobs.py (that is universal machinery touching every job in the pipeline, a materially bigger and costlier lever than this narrow message enrichment, and not measured as necessary here - a well-informed single re-ask may already be enough, per capability 3's own successful title-only fix in the very same attempt this run measured). NO relaxation of the slot-set rule, the title rule, or item 82's standard itself - explicitly the same guarantee E15/item 82 already committed to preserving.
